- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes; apply lagged smoothing: weight recent 3-day average more heavily than 7-day forecast.
- In 30-day horizon, model often overshoots late-period prices (especially after sentiment spike); cap forecast at 1.5–2% below true outcome’s final 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment volatility >0.8 SD from mean triggers “reversion penalty”: subtract 0.2–0.5% from forecast if sentiment swings sharply in 3–5 days.
